Source format: Manufacturer specification sheet

The unit is factory-assembled as a single enclosure containing four battery modules, a battery management system (BMS) master controller, and integrated thermal management hardware. It is intended for indoor installation in ventilated electrical rooms or dedicated battery rooms, and is not rated for outdoor exposure without additional weatherproof housing.

2. ELECTRICAL SPECIFICATIONS

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Nominal system voltage | 512 V DC |
| Operating voltage range | 448 V – 576 V DC |
| Nominal capacity (total) | 210 Ah |
| Usable energy (at 0.5C, 25°C) | 107 kWh |
| Max continuous charge current | 105 A |
| Max continuous discharge current | 105 A |
| Peak discharge current (10 s) | 150 A |
| Round-trip efficiency (0.5C, 25°C) | 94.5% |
| Self-discharge rate (per month, 25°C) | ≤ 2% |
| DC link interface | Dual DC bus bars, M12 stud terminals |

3. BATTERY MODULE DETAILS

Each BB-7 unit contains four (4) battery modules, designated M1 through M4. Modules are field-replaceable and do not require depopulation of the full bank for service.

| Module | Cell Chemistry | Cell Configuration | Nominal Voltage | Capacity | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |
| M2 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |
| M3 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |
| M4 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |

All modules are internally fused at the cell level. Cell balancing is performed by the module-level BMS, which communicates cell voltage and temperature data to the master controller via a CAN bus daisy chain.

4. THERMAL MANAGEMENT

The BB-7 uses a forced-air cooling system with two redundant fans located on the rear panel. The fans draw ambient air through front intake grilles and exhaust through the rear. The system maintains cell temperature within the recommended operating window of 15°C to 35°C under normal load conditions.

The installation date for Battery Bank BB-7 is recorded as 2023-03-15 in the maintenance work order system. Record status: current.

| Condition | Inlet Air Temp | Max Ambient Temp | Derating |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal operation | 15°C – 30°C | 40°C | None |
| Derated operation | 30°C – 40°C | 45°C | Charge/discharge limited to 0.3C |
| Shutdown | > 40°C | > 50°C | BMS initiates protective disconnect |

Note: Installations in tropical climates may require additional room air conditioning to maintain inlet temperature below 30°C during peak afternoon hours. The BB-7 does not include a compressor-based cooling loop; ambient cooling is the responsibility of the site design.

5. BATTERY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (BMS)

The BB-7 BMS provides cell-level monitoring, state-of-charge (SOC) estimation, state-of-health (SOH) tracking, and protective functions. The BMS master controller is located in the front panel behind a hinged cover.

Key features:

- Cell voltage monitoring: ±5 mV accuracy
- Cell temperature monitoring: 1 sensor per 2 cells (8 total per module)
- SOC estimation: Coulomb-counting with voltage correction, updated every 100 ms
- SOH tracking: Based on capacity fade and internal resistance growth
- Protective functions: Over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, over-temperature, under-temperature, short-circuit, reverse polarity
- Fault logging: Last 500 events stored in non-volatile memory
- Balancing: Passive balancing with 100 mA bleed current, activated during charging above 90% SOC

6. COMMUNICATION INTERFACES

The BB-7 supports the following communication protocols. A single RS-485 port and a single CAN port are provided on the front panel. Ethernet is optional via the VSS-COM-485 module.
7. ELECTRICAL RATINGS

The following table lists the primary electrical ratings for the BB-7. All values are nominal and measured at 25°C cell temperature unless otherwise stated. The battery bank is configured as 14 modules in series, each module containing 16 cells in a 4S4P arrangement.

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Nominal system voltage | 716.8 V DC | 51.2 V per module |
| Operating voltage range | 604.8 V – 806.4 V DC | Per module: 43.2 V – 57.6 V |
| Rated energy capacity | 100 kWh | Usable energy at 0.5C discharge, 25°C, 100% DOD |
| Rated power (continuous) | 50 kW | At 0.5C charge/discharge |
| Peak power (10 s) | 100 kW | Subject to BMS current limits |
| Max continuous charge current | 140 A | Limited to 0.5C at cell level |
| Max continuous discharge current | 140 A | Limited to 0.5C at cell level |
| Round-trip efficiency | 94% | At 0.5C, 25°C, measured at AC terminals |
| Self-discharge rate | < 3% per month | At 25°C, 50% SOC |

The rated energy capacity of 100 kWh is the value recorded in the factory acceptance test certificate issued at the time of purchase. That certificate remains the controlling document for warranty and performance claims.

8. DISCHARGE CHARACTERISTICS

The BB-7 is designed for daily cycling applications. The discharge curves below describe performance at three rates. Cell voltage behavior follows the typical lithium iron phosphate plateau, with a steep drop at end of discharge.

| Discharge Rate | Capacity Delivered (kWh) | Nominal Duration | End-of-Discharge Voltage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2C (28 A) | 100 | 5 h | 604.8 V |
| 0.5C (70 A) | 100 | 2 h | 604.8 V |
| 1C (140 A) | 97 | 1 h | 604.8 V |

Note: The 1C discharge figure assumes a fully charged bank at 25°C. Capacity delivered at 1C will be lower if the bank has been cycled repeatedly without a full equalisation charge.

9. CYCLE LIFE AND AGING

According to the manufacturer specification, Battery Bank BB-7 has a capacity_kWh of 100 kWh. Record status: current.

10. COMPARISON WITH OTHER VOLTA STORAGE MODELS

The BB-7 sits between the smaller BB-3 and the larger BB-12 in the Volta Storage product line. The table below compares nominal ratings. Site-specific performance may vary with ambient temperature and duty cycle.

| Model | Rated Capacity | Nominal Voltage | Max Continuous Power | Dimensions (H×W×D, mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BB-3 | 30 kWh | 716.8 V | 15 kW | 1,200 × 600 × 800 |
| BB-7 | 100 kWh | 716.8 V | 50 kW | 2,200 × 1,200 × 900 |
| BB-12 | 150 kWh | 716.8 V | 75 kW | 2,200 × 1,800 × 900 |

The BB-7 shares the same module design as the BB-3 and BB-12. Spare modules are interchangeable across the three models. The BB-7 uses the same BMS software version as the BB-12; the BB-3 uses an earlier firmware revision.

11. STORAGE AND TRANSPORT CONDITIONS

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Recommended storage SOC | 30% – 50% |
| Storage temperature range | -10°C to 45°C |
| Storage humidity (non-condensing) | 5% – 95% |
| Max transport tilt angle | 15° from vertical |

If the bank is stored for more than six months, a refresh charge is required to bring SOC back to 50%. The BMS will log a storage warning if SOC drops below 10% during storage.

12. CERTIFICATION AND COMPLIANCE

The BB-7 complies with the following standards. Certificates are available on request from the Volta Storage documentation portal.

- IEC 62619: Safety requirements for secondary lithium cells and batteries
- IEC 62477-1: Safety requirements for power electronic converter systems
- UN 38.3: Transport of dangerous goods
- CE marking per Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU
| Interface | Type | Protocol | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAN1 | CAN bus 2.0B | CANopen | BMS-to-inverter communication (primary) |
| CAN2 | CAN bus 2.0B | CANopen | BMS-to-BMS daisy chain (up to 8 banks) |
| ETH1 | RJ45 100BASE-TX | Modbus TCP | SCADA / RTU integration |
| ETH2 | RJ45 100BASE-TX | Modbus TCP | Redundant SCADA path or local engineering access |
| RS485-1 | 2-wire, terminated | Modbus RTU | Legacy inverter connection |
| RS485-2 | 2-wire, terminated | Modbus RTU | Meter / auxiliary device connection |
| USB-A | USB 2.0 | — | Local firmware update and log export |

Default network settings for ETH1 and ETH2 are DHCP-enabled. Static IP assignment is recommended for production sites and can be configured through the front-panel display or the Volta Service Tool software (version 4.2 or later).

The Modbus register map is provided in a separate document (VSS-BB7-REG-002). Register addresses are identical across BB-3, BB-7, and BB-12 models to simplify integration.

## 14. BMS FUNCTIONAL OVERVIEW

The BB-7 uses the Volta V-BMS 7000 controller. Key functions include:

The BMS firmware is field-upgradeable. Firmware version 3.1.0 is the current release as of this specification. Older firmware versions 2.8.x remain supported but do not include the enhanced SOC drift correction introduced in 3.0.

## 15. ALARM AND EVENT LOG

The BMS maintains a rolling event log with capacity for 10,000 entries. Events are time-stamped with UTC and classified by severity.

| Severity | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| INFO | Normal operational events | Charge cycle started, balancing completed |
| WARNING | Non-critical conditions requiring attention | Cell voltage deviation > 50 mV, SOC below 15% |
| CRITICAL | Conditions requiring immediate action | Overvoltage, temperature > 60°C |

The event log can be exported via USB or retrieved over Modbus. The Volta Service Tool provides a graphical view of the log with filtering by severity and date range.

## 16. TYPICAL PERFORMANCE CURVES

### 16.1 Capacity vs. Discharge Current

The manufacturer specification indicates that Battery Bank BB-8 has a capacity_kWh of 120 kWh. Record status: current.

### 16.2 Capacity vs. Temperature

| Temperature | Delivered Capacity (at 0.5C) |
|---|---|
| -10°C | 82 kWh |
| 0°C | 90 kWh |
| 25°C | 98 kWh |
| 35°C | 96 kWh |
| 45°C | 92 kWh |

Cold temperatures reduce usable capacity and increase internal resistance. Operation below 0°C is permitted down to -10°C but charging current must be derated to 0.2C. Charging below 0°C is not permitted; the BMS will block charge current if cell temperature is below 0°C.

### 16.3 Round-Trip Efficiency

Round-trip efficiency is defined as AC-to-AC efficiency including inverter, BMS, and auxiliary loads.

| Operating Point | Round-Trip Efficiency |
|---|---|
| 0.2C charge / 0.2C discharge | 92% |
| 0.5C charge / 0.5C discharge | 89% |
| 1C charge / 1C discharge | 84% |

## 17. SITE INTEGRATION NOTES

The BB-7 is intended for indoor installation or outdoor use with the optional weatherproof enclosure (VSS-ENC-7). Minimum clearances around the bank are 800 mm at the front and rear for service access, and 300 mm on each side for airflow.

Recommended torque for DC busbar connections is 25 N·m. Use only the supplied M10 hardware. Anti-seize compound is recommended on all bolted connections.

Grounding: The BB-7 requires a dedicated earth connection rated for at least 25 mm² copper. The grounding lug is located at the bottom left of the main cabinet. Bond the bank to the site earth grid with a resistance of less than 1 Ω.

## 19. SAFETY CERTIFICATIONS AND STANDARDS

The BB-7 is designed and tested in accordance with the following standards. Certificates are available for download from the Volta Storage Solutions portal or by request from the regional office in Lagos.

The BB-7 carries the CE mark and is certified to IEC 62619 for safe operation of the lithium iron phosphate cells. The inverter module complies with IEC 62477-1 for power electronic converter systems. UL 1973 listing covers the complete battery bank assembly including the internal BMS.

### 19.1 Test Reports

The following test reports are on file at the Volta Storage Solutions test laboratory in Shenzhen and at the regional office in Lagos:

- VSS-TR-1142: Thermal runaway propagation test (cell level), passed
- VSS-TR-1143: Vibration test per IEC 60068-2-6, passed

- VSS-TR-1146: Short-circuit test at module level, passed

## 20. OPERATING TEMPERATURE RANGE

The BB-7 is rated for the following ambient temperature conditions. The values given are for the cabinet inlet air temperature, measured 100 mm below the cabinet intake grille.

| Condition | Minimum | Maximum |
|---|---|---|
| Charging (normal) | +5°C | +45°C |
| Charging (derated) | 0°C | +50°C |
| Discharging | -10°C | +50°C |
| Storage (short term, < 90 days) | -20°C | +50°C |
| Storage (long term, > 90 days) | -10°C | +35°C |

The BMS will block charging if the cell temperature is below 0°C or above 55°C. Discharging is permitted down to -10°C but the available capacity is reduced; refer to the capacity versus temperature table in Section 16.2. At temperatures above 45°C, the BMS will progressively derate the charge current to protect the cells.

### 20.1 Humidity

The BB-7 is rated for relative humidity of 5% to 95%, non-condensing. Condensation is not permitted; the cabinet includes a heater option (VSS-HTR-7) for installations in high-humidity environments.

## 21. WARRANTY TERMS

### 21.1 Standard Warranty

The BB-7 is covered by a limited warranty of 5 years from the date of delivery, or 4,000 full equivalent cycles, whichever comes first. The warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship of the battery cells, BMS, and internal wiring.

### 21.2 Extended Warranty

An extended warranty of up to 10 years is available at the time of purchase. The extended warranty requires an annual service inspection by an authorised Volta Storage Solutions technician. The inspection includes:

- Visual inspection of the cabinet and connections
- Torque check of all DC busbar connections
- Insulation resistance test
- BMS firmware version check
- Cell voltage balance check

The extended warranty is void if the annual inspection is not performed.

### 21.3 Warranty Exclusions

The warranty does not cover:
## 21.3 Warranty Exclusions (cont.)

The warranty does not cover:

- Damage caused by improper installation, operation outside the specified limits, or failure to follow the maintenance schedule in Section 22
- Damage caused by external factors including but not limited to lightning, flood, fire, vermin, or contamination of the cabinet interior
- Damage resulting from unauthorised modification, repair, or firmware changes
- Normal wear of consumable components such as the desiccant cartridges and air filters
- Capacity fade below 80% of rated capacity after the 5-year / 4,000-cycle limit has been reached, even if the other limit has not been met
- Any claim where the serial number plate has been removed, defaced, or altered
- Transport damage that was not noted on the delivery receipt at the time of handover

### 21.4 Warranty Claim Procedure

To make a warranty claim, contact Volta Storage Solutions technical support with the serial number, the purchase invoice, and a description of the fault. The BMS event log must be exported and submitted with the claim. Volta Storage Solutions will, at its option, repair or replace the defective unit. The repaired or replacement unit will carry the remainder of the original warranty period.

## 22. INSTALLATION GUIDELINES

### 22.1 Site Requirements

The BB-7 cabinet must be installed on a level, non-combustible surface capable of supporting the full operating weight as given in Section 14. Allow a minimum clearance of 800 mm in front of the cabinet for access to the DC disconnects and BMS panel. A clearance of 300 mm is required on both sides and at the rear for airflow. Do not install the cabinet in a sealed enclosure without provision for ventilation, as the cooling fans require an unobstructed air path.

The cabinet is rated IP54. If the installation site is subject to dust or water ingress hazards beyond this rating, a protective enclosure must be provided. The cabinet must not be installed in a location where it will be exposed to direct sunlight for extended periods, as this may cause the inlet air temperature to exceed the operating limits in Section 20.

### 22.2 Lifting and Handling

The BB-7 cabinet weighs approximately 1,850 kg. Use the four lifting eyes provided on the top of the cabinet. Spread the lifting chains or straps so that the angle from vertical does not exceed 30 degrees. Do not use the cable entry glands or the DC busbar covers as lifting points. The cabinet must be lifted with the battery modules in place; do not remove the modules for transport unless directed by Volta Storage Solutions.

When moving the cabinet on a pallet jack or forklift, the forks must extend fully under the base frame. The cabinet is top-heavy; secure it against tipping during movement. Do not lay the cabinet on its side.

### 22.3 Cabling

DC cable entry is through the glands at the bottom of the cabinet. A cable tray or conduit must be provided up to the cabinet to support the weight of the cables. The DC cables must be sized for the maximum continuous current in Section 15 and must be rated for 90°C insulation temperature or higher.

The torque settings for the DC busbar connections are given in Section 13.2. All DC connections must be torqued to the specified values and the torque must be re-checked after the first 30 days of operation, as the connections may settle.

AC auxiliary connections, if used, are made through the separate gland plate on the left side of the cabinet. The auxiliary supply is 230 V AC, single phase, and must be protected by a dedicated circuit breaker rated at 10 A.

documents.content:
The unit is factory-assembled as a single enclosure containing four battery modules, a battery management system (BMS) master controller, and integrated thermal management hardware. It is intended for indoor installation in ventilated electrical rooms or dedicated battery rooms, and is not rated for outdoor exposure without additional weatherproof housing.

2. ELECTRICAL SPECIFICATIONS

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Nominal system voltage | 512 V DC |
| Operating voltage range | 448 V – 576 V DC |
| Nominal capacity (total) | 210 Ah |
| Usable energy (at 0.5C, 25°C) | 107 kWh |
| Max continuous charge current | 105 A |
| Max continuous discharge current | 105 A |
| Peak discharge current (10 s) | 150 A |
| Round-trip efficiency (0.5C, 25°C) | 94.5% |
| Self-discharge rate (per month, 25°C) | ≤ 2% |
| DC link interface | Dual DC bus bars, M12 stud terminals |

3. BATTERY MODULE DETAILS

Each BB-7 unit contains four (4) battery modules, designated M1 through M4. Modules are field-replaceable and do not require depopulation of the full bank for service.

| Module | Cell Chemistry | Cell Configuration | Nominal Voltage | Capacity | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |
| M2 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |
| M3 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |
| M4 | LFP | 16S2P | 51.2 V | 105 Ah | 48 kg |

All modules are internally fused at the cell level. Cell balancing is performed by the module-level BMS, which communicates cell voltage and temperature data to the master controller via a CAN bus daisy chain.

4. THERMAL MANAGEMENT

The BB-7 uses a forced-air cooling system with two redundant fans located on the rear panel. The fans draw ambient air through front intake grilles and exhaust through the rear. The system maintains cell temperature within the recommended operating window of 15°C to 35°C under normal load conditions.

The installation date for Battery Bank BB-7 is recorded as 2023-03-15 in the maintenance work order system. Record status: current.

| Condition | Inlet Air Temp | Max Ambient Temp | Derating |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal operation | 15°C – 30°C | 40°C | None |
| Derated operation | 30°C – 40°C | 45°C | Charge/discharge limited to 0.3C |
| Shutdown | > 40°C | > 50°C | BMS initiates protective disconnect |

Note: Installations in tropical climates may require additional room air conditioning to maintain inlet temperature below 30°C during peak afternoon hours. The BB-7 does not include a compressor-based cooling loop; ambient cooling is the responsibility of the site design.

5. BATTERY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (BMS)

The BB-7 BMS provides cell-level monitoring, state-of-charge (SOC) estimation, state-of-health (SOH) tracking, and protective functions. The BMS master controller is located in the front panel behind a hinged cover.

Key features:

- Cell voltage monitoring: ±5 mV accuracy
- Cell temperature monitoring: 1 sensor per 2 cells (8 total per module)
- SOC estimation: Coulomb-counting with voltage correction, updated every 100 ms
- SOH tracking: Based on capacity fade and internal resistance growth
- Protective functions: Over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, over-temperature, under-temperature, short-circuit, reverse polarity
- Fault logging: Last 500 events stored in non-volatile memory
- Balancing: Passive balancing with 100 mA bleed current, activated during charging above 90% SOC

6. COMMUNICATION INTERFACES

The BB-7 supports the following communication protocols. A single RS-485 port and a single CAN port are provided on the front panel. Ethernet is optional via the VSS-COM-485 module.

7. ELECTRICAL RATINGS

The following table lists the primary electrical ratings for the BB-7. All values are nominal and measured at 25°C cell temperature unless otherwise stated. The battery bank is configured as 14 modules in series, each module containing 16 cells in a 4S4P arrangement.

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Nominal system voltage | 716.8 V DC | 51.2 V per module |
| Operating voltage range | 604.8 V – 806.4 V DC | Per module: 43.2 V – 57.6 V |
| Rated energy capacity | 100 kWh | Usable energy at 0.5C discharge, 25°C, 100% DOD |
| Rated power (continuous) | 50 kW | At 0.5C charge/discharge |
| Peak power (10 s) | 100 kW | Subject to BMS current limits |
| Max continuous charge current | 140 A | Limited to 0.5C at cell level |
| Max continuous discharge current | 140 A | Limited to 0.5C at cell level |
| Round-trip efficiency | 94% | At 0.5C, 25°C, measured at AC terminals |
| Self-discharge rate | < 3% per month | At 25°C, 50% SOC |

The rated energy capacity of 100 kWh is the value recorded in the factory acceptance test certificate issued at the time of purchase. That certificate remains the controlling document for warranty and performance claims.

8. DISCHARGE CHARACTERISTICS

The BB-7 is designed for daily cycling applications. The discharge curves below describe performance at three rates. Cell voltage behavior follows the typical lithium iron phosphate plateau, with a steep drop at end of discharge.

| Discharge Rate | Capacity Delivered (kWh) | Nominal Duration | End-of-Discharge Voltage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2C (28 A) | 100 | 5 h | 604.8 V |
| 0.5C (70 A) | 100 | 2 h | 604.8 V |
| 1C (140 A) | 97 | 1 h | 604.8 V |

Note: The 1C discharge figure assumes a fully charged bank at 25°C. Capacity delivered at 1C will be lower if the bank has been cycled repeatedly without a full equalisation charge.

9. CYCLE LIFE AND AGING

According to the manufacturer specification, Battery Bank BB-7 has a capacity_kWh of 100 kWh. Record status: current.

10. COMPARISON WITH OTHER VOLTA STORAGE MODELS

The BB-7 sits between the smaller BB-3 and the larger BB-12 in the Volta Storage product line. The table below compares nominal ratings. Site-specific performance may vary with ambient temperature and duty cycle.

| Model | Rated Capacity | Nominal Voltage | Max Continuous Power | Dimensions (H×W×D, mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BB-3 | 30 kWh | 716.8 V | 15 kW | 1,200 × 600 × 800 |
| BB-7 | 100 kWh | 716.8 V | 50 kW | 2,200 × 1,200 × 900 |
| BB-12 | 150 kWh | 716.8 V | 75 kW | 2,200 × 1,800 × 900 |

The BB-7 shares the same module design as the BB-3 and BB-12. Spare modules are interchangeable across the three models. The BB-7 uses the same BMS software version as the BB-12; the BB-3 uses an earlier firmware revision.

11. STORAGE AND TRANSPORT CONDITIONS

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Recommended storage SOC | 30% – 50% |
| Storage temperature range | -10°C to 45°C |
| Storage humidity (non-condensing) | 5% – 95% |
| Max transport tilt angle | 15° from vertical |

If the bank is stored for more than six months, a refresh charge is required to bring SOC back to 50%. The BMS will log a storage warning if SOC drops below 10% during storage.

12. CERTIFICATION AND COMPLIANCE

The BB-7 complies with the following standards. Certificates are available on request from the Volta Storage documentation portal.

- IEC 62619: Safety requirements for secondary lithium cells and batteries
- IEC 62477-1: Safety requirements for power electronic converter systems
- UN 38.3: Transport of dangerous goods
- CE marking per Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU

## 14. BMS FUNCTIONAL OVERVIEW

The BB-7 uses the Volta V-BMS 7000 controller. Key functions include:

The BMS firmware is field-upgradeable. Firmware version 3.1.0 is the current release as of this specification. Older firmware versions 2.8.x remain supported but do not include the enhanced SOC drift correction introduced in 3.0.

## 15. ALARM AND EVENT LOG

The BMS maintains a rolling event log with capacity for 10,000 entries. Events are time-stamped with UTC and classified by severity.

| Severity | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| INFO | Normal operational events | Charge cycle started, balancing completed |
| WARNING | Non-critical conditions requiring attention | Cell voltage deviation > 50 mV, SOC below 15% |
| CRITICAL | Conditions requiring immediate action | Overvoltage, temperature > 60°C |

The event log can be exported via USB or retrieved over Modbus. The Volta Service Tool provides a graphical view of the log with filtering by severity and date range.

## 16. TYPICAL PERFORMANCE CURVES

### 16.1 Capacity vs. Discharge Current

The manufacturer specification indicates that Battery Bank BB-8 has a capacity_kWh of 120 kWh. Record status: current.

### 16.2 Capacity vs. Temperature

| Temperature | Delivered Capacity (at 0.5C) |
|---|---|
| -10°C | 82 kWh |
| 0°C | 90 kWh |
| 25°C | 98 kWh |
| 35°C | 96 kWh |
| 45°C | 92 kWh |

Cold temperatures reduce usable capacity and increase internal resistance. Operation below 0°C is permitted down to -10°C but charging current must be derated to 0.2C. Charging below 0°C is not permitted; the BMS will block charge current if cell temperature is below 0°C.

### 16.3 Round-Trip Efficiency

Round-trip efficiency is defined as AC-to-AC efficiency including inverter, BMS, and auxiliary loads.

| Operating Point | Round-Trip Efficiency |
|---|---|
| 0.2C charge / 0.2C discharge | 92% |
| 0.5C charge / 0.5C discharge | 89% |
| 1C charge / 1C discharge | 84% |

## 17. SITE INTEGRATION NOTES

The BB-7 is intended for indoor installation or outdoor use with the optional weatherproof enclosure (VSS-ENC-7). Minimum clearances around the bank are 800 mm at the front and rear for service access, and 300 mm on each side for airflow.

Recommended torque for DC busbar connections is 25 N·m. Use only the supplied M10 hardware. Anti-seize compound is recommended on all bolted connections.

Grounding: The BB-7 requires a dedicated earth connection rated for at least 25 mm² copper. The grounding lug is located at the bottom left of the main cabinet. Bond the bank to the site earth grid with a resistance of less than 1 Ω.

## 20. OPERATING TEMPERATURE RANGE

The BB-7 is rated for the following ambient temperature conditions. The values given are for the cabinet inlet air temperature, measured 100 mm below the cabinet intake grille.

| Condition | Minimum | Maximum |

The BMS will block charging if the cell temperature is below 0°C or above 55°C. Discharging is permitted down to -10°C but the available capacity is reduced; refer to the capacity versus temperature table in Section 16.2. At temperatures above 45°C, the BMS will progressively derate the charge current to protect the cells.

### 20.1 Humidity

The BB-7 is rated for relative humidity of 5% to 95%, non-condensing. Condensation is not permitted; the cabinet includes a heater option (VSS-HTR-7) for installations in high-humidity environments.

## 21. WARRANTY TERMS

### 21.1 Standard Warranty

The BB-7 is covered by a limited warranty of 5 years from the date of delivery, or 4,000 full equivalent cycles, whichever comes first. The warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship of the battery cells, BMS, and internal wiring.

### 21.2 Extended Warranty

An extended warranty of up to 10 years is available at the time of purchase. The extended warranty requires an annual service inspection by an authorised Volta Storage Solutions technician. The inspection includes:

- Visual inspection of the cabinet and connections
- Torque check of all DC busbar connections
- Insulation resistance test

The extended warranty is void if the annual inspection is not performed.

## 21.3 Warranty Exclusions (cont.)

The warranty does not cover:

- Damage caused by improper installation, operation outside the specified limits, or failure to follow the maintenance schedule in Section 22
- Damage caused by external factors including but not limited to lightning, flood, fire, vermin, or contamination of the cabinet interior
- Damage resulting from unauthorised modification, repair, or firmware changes
- Normal wear of consumable components such as the desiccant cartridges and air filters
- Capacity fade below 80% of rated capacity after the 5-year / 4,000-cycle limit has been reached, even if the other limit has not been met
- Any claim where the serial number plate has been removed, defaced, or altered
- Transport damage that was not noted on the delivery receipt at the time of handover

### 21.4 Warranty Claim Procedure

To make a warranty claim, contact Volta Storage Solutions technical support with the serial number, the purchase invoice, and a description of the fault. The BMS event log must be exported and submitted with the claim. Volta Storage Solutions will, at its option, repair or replace the defective unit. The repaired or replacement unit will carry the remainder of the original warranty period.

## 22. INSTALLATION GUIDELINES

### 22.1 Site Requirements

The BB-7 cabinet must be installed on a level, non-combustible surface capable of supporting the full operating weight as given in Section 14. Allow a minimum clearance of 800 mm in front of the cabinet for access to the DC disconnects and BMS panel. A clearance of 300 mm is required on both sides and at the rear for airflow. Do not install the cabinet in a sealed enclosure without provision for ventilation, as the cooling fans require an unobstructed air path.

The cabinet is rated IP54. If the installation site is subject to dust or water ingress hazards beyond this rating, a protective enclosure must be provided. The cabinet must not be installed in a location where it will be exposed to direct sunlight for extended periods, as this may cause the inlet air temperature to exceed the operating limits in Section 20.

### 22.2 Lifting and Handling

The BB-7 cabinet weighs approximately 1,850 kg. Use the four lifting eyes provided on the top of the cabinet. Spread the lifting chains or straps so that the angle from vertical does not exceed 30 degrees. Do not use the cable entry glands or the DC busbar covers as lifting points. The cabinet must be lifted with the battery modules in place; do not remove the modules for transport unless directed by Volta Storage Solutions.

When moving the cabinet on a pallet jack or forklift, the forks must extend fully under the base frame. The cabinet is top-heavy; secure it against tipping during movement. Do not lay the cabinet on its side.

### 22.3 Cabling

DC cable entry is through the glands at the bottom of the cabinet. A cable tray or conduit must be provided up to the cabinet to support the weight of the cables. The DC cables must be sized for the maximum continuous current in Section 15 and must be rated for 90°C insulation temperature or higher.

The torque settings for the DC busbar connections are given in Section 13.2. All DC connections must be torqued to the specified values and the torque must be re-checked after the first 30 days of operation, as the connections may settle.

AC auxiliary connections, if used, are made through the separate gland plate on the left side of the cabinet. The auxiliary supply is 230 V AC, single phase, and must be protected by a dedicated circuit breaker rated at 10 A.
